description: WHM token and session management, application inventory and legacy API usage reads. Returned credentials, identifiers and URLs are private payload data.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 64.
Requires HTTPS. Names are unique, at most 50 alphanumeric/dash/underscore characters; root cannot use WebPros_Dashboard or WP-Dashboard.

Omitted acl assigns all caller privileges; only caller-held privileges may be assigned. Omitted expiration or zero means no expiration; expired tokens require manual revocation. Omitted whitelist permits any IP.
The returned token is a secret shown only once.
Store the returned credential securely and never log the result.
ACL prose and examples use acl-0/acl-1. Whitelist prose uses whitelist_ip-0/whitelist_ip-1, while later example keys switch to whitelist-ip; these source limitations remain unresolved.

Typed acl and whitelistIp accept one scalar and cannot create or preserve multiple ACL or IP values. Multi-value support is deferred under 8x0.1.21; the existing unsuffixed-first numbered encoding does not represent these indexed families and is not used here.

An accepted creation outcome can still raise PayloadMismatchException after the credential was created. Its sensitive unvalidated $payload may contain the only returned secret, but a malformed payload need not contain it. Recover it securely if present and revoke the created named credential through an authorized caller action. Never automatically retry, log the payload or automatically revoke a credential.
Uses form POST under the client mutation transport policy to keep operation parameters out of access-log URLs.

evidence.note: Pinned operation is x-readonly=false and creates, changes or revokes authentication state; use form POST per the reviewed mutation transport convention.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 98.
The token input is the raw secret, not its name.
Recognized tokens return TokenDetails; the unrecognized alternative omits data. TokenDetails has no required fields. Optional nullable fields remain distinct from omission.

The raw token input is sensitive and sent in a form POST to keep it out of access-log URLs; pinned GET-to-POST compatibility remains live-unverified. Treat returned token settings as private payload data.
Absent or explicit null data returns null. A present empty object remains an empty result; it is unobserved and does not prove recognition or establish an invalid-token signal.

evidence.note: The documented token parameter is the raw API secret. Existing sensitive-input transport policy uses a conservative form POST to keep secrets out of URLs; POST compatibility remains live-unverified. Top-level anyOf documents Token Recognized data as allOf(description, TokenDetails reference) and Token Unrecognized without data; optional_payload preserves both alternatives.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 68.

ACL and whitelist inputs replace all current settings. Pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration; zero also means no expiration. Only caller-held privileges may be assigned. whitelistIp=any explicitly clears IP restrictions. Expired tokens require manual revocation.

The typed method requires explicit acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt to express the complete replacement settings, including when renaming. Empty strings are not a documented way to preserve current settings.
Omitted newName preserves the name; replacements must be unique and at most 50 alphanumeric/dash/underscore characters. Root cannot rename to WebPros_Dashboard, WP-Dashboard or Platform360.
ACL prose uses acl-1/acl-2 but its example uses acl-0/acl-1; whitelist prose uses whitelist_ip-0 while later example keys use whitelist-ip. These source limitations remain unresolved.

Typed acl and whitelistIp accept one scalar and cannot preserve or create multiple ACL or IP values. Do not use updateToken to rename a token restricted by multiple ACL or IP values. Multi-value support is deferred under 8x0.1.21; the existing unsuffixed-first numbered encoding is not used for these families. Treat returned settings as private payload data.
Uses form POST under the client mutation transport policy to keep operation parameters out of access-log URLs.

token_name.description: The existing API token name. This replaces complete settings, including for a rename: pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. The client requires acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt explicitly; empty strings are not documented preservation values.

acl.description: The complete replacement privilege, limited to caller-held privileges. This replaces complete settings, including for a rename: pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. The client requires acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt explicitly; empty strings are not documented preservation values.

whitelist_ip.description: The complete replacement remote IP or CIDR range; any explicitly clears IP restrictions. This replaces complete settings, including for a rename: pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. The client requires acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt explicitly; empty strings are not documented preservation values.

expires_at.description: The replacement Unix expiration time; zero explicitly means no expiration. Expired tokens require manual revocation. This replaces complete settings, including for a rename: pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. The client requires acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt explicitly; empty strings are not documented preservation values.

new_name.description: The optional new unique name, at most 50 alphanumeric/dash/underscore characters; omission preserves the name. Root cannot use WebPros_Dashboard, WP-Dashboard or Platform360. This replaces complete settings, including for a rename: pinned omission assigns all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. The client requires acl, whitelistIp and expiresAt explicitly; empty strings are not documented preservation values.

The api_token_update parameter descriptions explicitly replace all ACL and whitelist settings; omission grants all caller privileges, permits any IP and removes expiration. Require the three settings as non-null inputs by client safety policy, ordered token_name, acl, whitelist_ip, expires_at, new_name. Scalar indexed-family support remains deferred; no undocumented empty-string preservation contract is introduced. notes.text: Available from cPanel 11.40.
Creates a temporary session for cpaneld, whostmgrd or webmaild and the supplied account username or valid email address. The system destroys temporary sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.

Omitted app is blank and targets cPanel Home; an invalid application still creates a session without linking the application. Omitted locale uses Server Locale; an explicit locale sends a one-year browser cookie. preferredDomain defaults to the server hostname.
cpSecurityToken is a session secret. promptToken contains base64 website-generation goals with maximum decoded length 5000.

Session identifiers, security tokens and URLs are private opaque payload strings; never log them or retrieve the returned URL. cpSecurityToken and promptToken inputs are sensitive when accepted by the operation.
Uses form POST under the client mutation transport policy to keep operation parameters out of access-log URLs.

Returns registered cPanel, Webmail and WHM application lists, preserving optional AppConfig fields. displayname, entryurl, icon, origin, target and upgradecall are documented only for AppConfig-registered plugins.
